children: By Johann M Cherian and Anjana Jayakrishnan Nair

Europe's STOXX 600 index opened higher and traded near record highs on Wednesday, as strong forecasts from Siemens Energy and US-based CoreWeave helped ease concerns about the AI trade outlook, while inflation worries kept a lid on gains.
gained 0.7% to 662.83 points by 0807 GMT and was just a whisker away from breaching record levels reached in August.
gained 6.5% on expectations of higher profit margins in 2027. The company announced plans to more than triple its dividend.
Shares of its peers Schneider Electric
gained around 2.6%, while the broader tech sector (.SX8P) added 1.7%.
said it would become profitable on an adjusted basis in the first half of 2028.
Among laggards on the STOXX index, wind turbine operator Vestas
fell 6%, after reporting third-quarter operating profit below market estimates.
Czech-based ammunition and arms producer CSG
tanked 18% after cutting its full-year operating margin forecast.
A rebound in Brent crude prices

following shipping attacks in the Strait of Hormuz stoked some caution, a day after hotter-than-expected US inflation data lifted expectations for a December interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve.
